passages.text: Of David.
passages.sermon: David wrote this psalm.\r\nDavid is the author.\r\nDavid speaks to God in this psalm.

passages.text: Contend with my opponents, O LORD; fight against those who fight against me.
passages.sermon: David speaks to the LORD.\r\nDavid asks the LORD to contend with his opponents.\r\nDavid asks the LORD to fight against those who fight against him.
passages.original: לְדָוִ֨ד׀ רִיבָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה אֶת־ יְרִיבַ֑י לְ֝חַ֗ם אֶת־ לֹֽחֲמָֽי׃

passages.text: Take up Your shield and buckler; arise and come to my aid.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to the LORD.
David asks God to help him.
David says, “God, take up Your shield and buckler.”
David says, “God, stand up and help me.”
passages.original: הַחֲזֵ֣ק מָגֵ֣ן וְצִנָּ֑ה וְ֝ק֗וּמָה בְּעֶזְרָתִֽי׃

passages.text: Draw the spear and javelin against my pursuers; say to my soul: “I am your salvation.”
passages.sermon:
God, you are my defender.
My enemies chase me.
Take your spear and javelin.
Stand against those who pursue me.
Speak to my soul.
Say, “I am your salvation.”
passages.original: וְהָ֘רֵ֤ק חֲנִ֣ית וּ֭סְגֹר לִקְרַ֣את רֹדְפָ֑י אֱמֹ֥ר לְ֝נַפְשִׁ֗י יְֽשֻׁעָתֵ֥ךְ אָֽנִי׃

passages.text: May those who seek my life be disgraced and put to shame; may those who plan to harm me be driven back and confounded.
passages.sermon:
This passage is a prayer to God for protection from enemies.
The speaker asks God to act against those who want to harm him.
Some people seek to take the speaker’s life.
May these people feel disgrace.
May these people feel shame.
Other people plan evil against the speaker.
May these people turn back.
May these people feel confusion.
passages.original: יֵבֹ֣שׁוּ וְיִכָּלְמוּ֮ מְבַקְשֵׁ֪י נַ֫פְשִׁ֥י יִסֹּ֣גוּ אָח֣וֹר וְיַחְפְּר֑וּ חֹ֝שְׁבֵ֗י רָעָתִֽי׃

passages.text: May they be like chaff in the wind, as the angel of the LORD drives them away.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks about his enemies.
He asks God to act against them.
He says, “Let them be like chaff before the wind.”
Chaff is light and worthless.
The wind blows chaff away easily.
He asks the angel of the LORD to drive them away.
The angel of the LORD is God’s messenger and servant.
The angel acts with God’s power.
The psalmist wants his enemies removed quickly and completely.
passages.original: יִֽהְי֗וּ כְּמֹ֥ץ לִפְנֵי־ ר֑וּחַ וּמַלְאַ֖ךְ יְהוָ֣ה דּוֹחֶֽה׃

passages.text: May their path be dark and slick, as the angel of the LORD pursues.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks about his enemies.
His enemies want to harm him.
He asks God to act against them.
He says, "Let their path be dark."
He says, "Let their path be slippery."
He says, "Let the angel of the LORD chase them."
passages.original: יְֽהִי־ דַרְכָּ֗ם חֹ֥שֶׁךְ וַחֲלַקְלַקּ֑וֹת וּמַלְאַ֥ךְ יְ֝הוָ֗ה רֹדְפָֽם׃

passages.text: For without cause they laid their net for me; without reason they dug a pit for my soul.
passages.sermon:
My enemies acted without cause.
They set a trap for me.
They laid their net to catch me.
They had no reason to do this.
They dug a pit to harm my soul.
They did this without justification.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ חִנָּ֣ם טָֽמְנוּ־ לִ֭י שַׁ֣חַת רִשְׁתָּ֑ם חִ֝נָּ֗ם חָפְר֥וּ לְנַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: May ruin befall them by surprise; may the net they hid ensnare them; may they fall into the hazard they created.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks about his enemies.
He asks that disaster come upon them suddenly.
He wants them to be caught by surprise.
He says they have hidden a net to trap others.
He asks that their own net trap them instead.
He wants them to fall into the danger they made for others.
passages.original: תְּבוֹאֵ֣הוּ שׁוֹאָה֮ לֹֽא־ יֵ֫דָ֥ע וְרִשְׁתּ֣וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ טָמַ֣ן תִּלְכְּד֑וֹ בְּ֝שׁוֹאָ֗ה יִפָּל־ בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: Then my soul will rejoice in the LORD and exult in His salvation.
passages.sermon: My soul will rejoice in the LORD.\r\nMy soul will exult in His salvation.
passages.original: וְ֭נַפְשִׁי תָּגִ֣יל בַּיהוָ֑ה תָּ֝שִׂישׂ בִּישׁוּעָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: All my bones will exclaim, “Who is like You, O LORD, who delivers the afflicted from the aggressor, the poor and needy from the robber?”
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a person who trusts in the LORD.
The speaker says every part of their body will speak.
The speaker says, "LORD, who is like You?"
The LORD saves people who are afflicted.
The LORD rescues the weak from those who are stronger than they are.
The LORD delivers the poor and needy from those who rob them.
passages.original: כָּ֥ל עַצְמוֹתַ֨י׀ תֹּאמַרְנָה֮ יְהוָ֗ה מִ֥י כָ֫מ֥וֹךָ מַצִּ֣יל עָ֭נִי מֵחָזָ֣ק מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וְעָנִ֥י וְ֝אֶבְי֗וֹן מִגֹּזְלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Hostile witnesses come forward; they make charges I know nothing about.
passages.sermon:
Hostile people stand up as witnesses against me.
They accuse me.
I do not know them.
They ask me about things I do not know.
passages.original: יְ֭קוּמוּן עֵדֵ֣י חָמָ֑ס אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ יָ֝דַ֗עְתִּי יִשְׁאָלֽוּנִי׃

passages.text: They repay me evil for good, to the bereavement of my soul.
passages.sermon:
My enemies repay me with evil.
I have done good to them.
They give me harm instead of kindness.
Their actions cause deep sorrow in my soul.
I feel as if I have lost something precious.
passages.original: יְשַׁלְּמ֣וּנִי רָ֭עָה תַּ֥חַת טוֹבָ֗ה שְׁכ֣וֹל לְנַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: Yet when they were ill, I put on sackcloth; I humbled myself with fasting, but my prayers returned unanswered.
passages.sermon:
My enemies became sick.
I saw their suffering.
I put on sackcloth to show my sorrow.
I humbled myself by fasting.
I prayed for them.
My prayers came back to me without answer.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֤י׀ בַּחֲלוֹתָ֡ם לְב֬וּשִׁי שָׂ֗ק עִנֵּ֣יתִי בַצּ֣וֹם נַפְשִׁ֑י וּ֝תְפִלָּתִ֗י עַל־ חֵיקִ֥י תָשֽׁוּב׃

passages.text: I paced about as for my friend or brother; I was bowed down with grief, like one mourning for his mother.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is David.
David acted with kindness and care.
David treated others as if they were his close friend.
David treated others as if they were his own brother.
David walked among them with compassion.
David felt deep sorrow.
David mourned as one who grieves for his mother.
David’s grief was heavy and dark.
passages.original: כְּרֵֽעַ־ כְּאָ֣ח לִ֭י הִתְהַלָּ֑כְתִּי כַּאֲבֶל־ אֵ֝֗ם קֹדֵ֥ר שַׁחֽוֹתִי׃

passages.text: But when I stumbled, they assembled in glee; they gathered together against me. Assailants I did not know slandered me without ceasing.
passages.sermon:
Enemies attacked me.
I did not know these enemies.
I stumbled.
They saw my trouble.
They became happy.
They gathered together.
They gathered against me.
They tore at me.
They did not stop.
They slandered me again and again.
passages.original: וּבְצַלְעִי֮ שָׂמְח֪וּ וְֽנֶאֱ֫סָ֥פוּ נֶאֶסְפ֬וּ עָלַ֣י נֵ֭כִים וְלֹ֣א יָדַ֑עְתִּי קָֽרְע֥וּ וְלֹא־ דָֽמּוּ׃

passages.text: Like godless jesters at a feast, they gnashed their teeth at me.
passages.sermon:
My enemies acted like jesters at a feast.
They had no respect for God.
They mocked me openly.
They gnashed their teeth at me.
They showed their anger and hatred clearly.
passages.original: בְּ֭חַנְפֵי לַעֲגֵ֣י מָע֑וֹג חָרֹ֖ק עָלַ֣י שִׁנֵּֽימוֹ׃

passages.text: How long, O Lord, will You look on? Rescue my soul from their ravages, my precious life from these lions.
passages.sermon:
O Lord, you are watching me.
How long will you only look?
Enemies attack me.
They try to destroy me.
They are like lions.
Save my soul from their harm.
Save my precious life from these lions.
passages.original: אֲדֹנָי֮ כַּמָּ֪ה תִּ֫רְאֶ֥ה הָשִׁ֣יבָה נַ֭פְשִׁי מִשֹּׁאֵיהֶ֑ם מִ֝כְּפִירִ֗ים יְחִידָתִֽי׃

passages.text: Then I will give You thanks in the great assembly; I will praise You among many people.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David promises to thank God.
He will thank God in a great assembly.
He will praise God among many people.
passages.original: א֭וֹדְךָ בְּקָהָ֣ל רָ֑ב בְּעַ֖ם עָצ֣וּם אֲהַֽלְלֶֽךָּ׃

passages.text: Let not my enemies gloat over me without cause, nor those who hate me without reason wink in malice.
passages.sermon:
My enemies hate me for no reason.
They are not honest.
Do not let them gloat over me.
Some people hate me without cause.
Do not let them wink at me in malice.
passages.original: אַֽל־ יִשְׂמְחוּ־ לִ֣י אֹיְבַ֣י שֶׁ֑קֶר שֹׂנְאַ֥י חִ֝נָּ֗ם יִקְרְצוּ־ עָֽיִן׃

passages.text: For they do not speak peace, but they devise deceitful schemes against those who live quietly in the land.
passages.sermon:
My enemies do not speak words of peace.
They speak words that cause trouble.
They plan deceitful schemes.
They make these plans against people who live quietly in the land.
These quiet people do not seek conflict.
My enemies target them with lies and trickery.
passages.original: כִּ֤י לֹ֥א שָׁל֗וֹם יְדַ֫בֵּ֥רוּ וְעַ֥ל רִגְעֵי־ אֶ֑רֶץ דִּבְרֵ֥י מִ֝רְמוֹת יַחֲשֹׁבֽוּן׃

passages.text: They gape at me and say, “Aha, aha! Our eyes have seen!”
passages.sermon:
My enemies open their mouths wide against me.
They look at me and mock me.
They say, “Aha, aha!”
They claim, “Our eyes have seen it.”
passages.original: וַיַּרְחִ֥יבוּ עָלַ֗י פִּ֫יהֶ֥ם אָ֭מְרוּ הֶאָ֣ח׀ הֶאָ֑ח רָאֲתָ֥ה עֵינֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: O LORD, You have seen it; be not silent. O Lord, be not far from me.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD sees everything.
The LORD has seen what happened.
I ask the LORD not to stay silent.
I call to the Lord and say, do not be far from me.
passages.original: רָאִ֣יתָה יְ֭הוָה אַֽל־ תֶּחֱרַ֑שׁ אֲ֝דֹנָ֗י אֲל־ תִּרְחַ֥ק מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

passages.text: Awake and rise to my defense, to my cause, my God and my Lord!
passages.sermon:
God is my defender.
God is my Lord.
I ask God to awake.
I ask God to rise up.
I ask God to help me in my case.
I ask God to stand for my cause.
passages.original: הָעִ֣ירָה וְ֭הָקִיצָה לְמִשְׁפָּטִ֑י אֱלֹהַ֖י וַֽאדֹנָ֣י לְרִיבִֽי׃

passages.text: Vindicate me by Your righteousness, O LORD my God, and do not let them gloat over me.
passages.sermon:
O LORD, you are my God.
You are righteous.
Judge me according to your righteousness.
Do not let my enemies rejoice over me.
passages.original: שָׁפְטֵ֣נִי כְ֭צִדְקְךָ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָ֗י וְאַל־ יִשְׂמְחוּ־ לִֽי׃

passages.text: Let them not say in their hearts, “Aha, just what we wanted!” Let them not say, “We have swallowed him up!”
passages.sermon:
The speaker prays to God for protection from enemies.
The speaker asks God to stop the enemies from thinking evil thoughts.
The speaker says, “Do not let them say in their hearts, ‘Aha, just what we wanted!’”
The speaker says, “Do not let them say, ‘We have swallowed him up!’”
passages.original: אַל־ יֹאמְר֣וּ בְ֭לִבָּם הֶאָ֣ח נַפְשֵׁ֑נוּ אַל־ יֹ֝אמְר֗וּ בִּֽלַּעֲנֽוּהוּ׃

passages.text: May those who gloat in my distress be ashamed and confounded; may those who exalt themselves over me be clothed in shame and reproach.
passages.sermon:
David is the servant of the LORD.
David speaks to God.
Some people gloat when David suffers.
These people feel joy in David’s distress.
Some people exalt themselves over David.
David asks God to act.
David asks God to make those who gloat in his distress feel ashamed.
David asks God to make them feel confused.
David asks God to cover those who exalt themselves over him with shame.
David asks God to clothe them with reproach.
passages.original: יֵ֘בֹ֤שׁוּ וְיַחְפְּר֨וּ׀ יַחְדָּו֮ שְׂמֵחֵ֪י רָעָ֫תִ֥י יִֽלְבְּשׁוּ־ בֹ֥שֶׁת וּכְלִמָּ֑ה הַֽמַּגְדִּילִ֥ים עָלָֽי׃

passages.text: May those who favor my vindication shout for joy and gladness; may they always say, “Exalted be the LORD who delights in His servant’s well-being.”
passages.sermon:
David is the servant of the LORD.
Some people want David to be proven right.
These people support David’s vindication.
Let these people shout for joy.
Let them be glad.
Let them always say, “The LORD is great.”
The LORD delights in the well-being of His servant.
passages.original: יָרֹ֣נּוּ וְיִשְׂמְחוּ֮ חֲפֵצֵ֪י צִ֫דְקִ֥י וְיֹאמְר֣וּ תָ֭מִיד יִגְדַּ֣ל יְהוָ֑ה הֶ֝חָפֵ֗ץ שְׁל֣וֹם עַבְדּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then my tongue will proclaim Your righteousness and Your praises all day long.
passages.sermon:
David is the servant of the LORD.
David speaks to God.
David says, "My tongue will proclaim Your righteousness."
I will speak about Your righteousness.
I will praise You all day long.
My mouth will declare Your praise without stopping.
passages.original: וּ֭לְשׁוֹנִי תֶּהְגֶּ֣ה צִדְקֶ֑ךָ כָּל־ הַ֝יּוֹם תְּהִלָּתֶֽךָ׃
